newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa rises, March delivery talking point.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa rises, March delivery talking point.

text.p: Cocoa prices extended their gains on Thursday, taking their cue from a rebound in New York and as the looming March expiry injected some nervousness, traders said.
A few were speculating on a reasonable delivery onto March given that the uncovered open interest still stands above 6,000 lots just two sessions before the first notice day on Monday.
The spot discount has already narrowed to around 20 stg at one stage and some traders see scope for a further squeeze to 15.
"If he (a trader said to have gone long of March) is long and he holds off the cocoa from March, who else is going to deliver?" said one trader. "We may have quite a nervous period on Monday."
But other players were more relaxed, taking comfort in relatively abundant supplies and expecting the open interest to continue to shrink with a steady flow of price fixation.
The March conract traded six stg higher on the day at 871 stg a tonne after a high of 875, while the second-month May finished morning dealings at 895 stg, up nine, after touching 890.
Traders said a close on May above 900 stg would be seen encouraging and could begin to pave the way for short covering.
The market's technical prospects seem to have improved since Wednesday's encouraging close but analysts say the rise needs to gather further momentum for prices to break out of their range.
May has an initial target of 914-922, a gap on charts, followed by the key resistance level of 938.
"The market has absorbed a lot of origin selling. If it begins to move up I don't see where the selling will come from. There is a lot of pent up buying in the market," said one trader.
But buffer stock sales by the International Cocoa Organization (ICCO) for February, expected on Friday since there have been no sales so far this month, could put a dampener on the rally.
The midsession turnover totalled 4,696 lots. This included 1,000 lots of March against actuals, traders said. -- Clelia Oziel, London Newsroom +44-171-542 8072
